title: The Impatience Spiral
coreMove: Impatience loosens when you stop using speed to crush anxiety and practice one next action at reality's pace, even while the urge to rush keeps shouting.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a genuine speed win can become a new anxiety floor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show James Gleick, Faster, rush, and speed culture turning a win into pressure

exampleSpecs.audience: health staff facing anxious response loops
exampleSpecs.stakes: patient care suffers when hurry pretends to be control
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Stephanie Brown, speed addiction, clients, and anxiety in a refresh loop

exampleSpecs.domain: small business owner in a recovery meeting
exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse surrender with giving up
exampleSpecs.stakes: a false control project can keep daily life unmanageable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Alcoholics Anonymous, Twelve Steps, First Step, and powerlessness without equating hurry with alcohol

exampleSpecs.audience: creative workers pushing slow work too hard
exampleSpecs.stakes: rushing can damage the very sentence the worker wants to improve
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Stephanie Brown, speed addiction, clients, and anxiety in a slow craft scene

exampleSpecs.audience: project coordinators surrounded by urgent messages
exampleSpecs.stakes: one real deadline can make every thread feel equally urgent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show James Gleick, Faster, rush, and speed culture in a message storm

exampleSpecs.stakes: panic can turn a repairable delay into a demand for magic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Alcoholics Anonymous, Twelve Steps, First Step, and powerlessness in an operations setting
